records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And it came about in the being him in a certain place praying, when he ceased, said one of the disciples of him to him, Lord, teach us to pray, just as also John taught the disciples of him.
pieces: Once Jesus was praying in a certain place. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had finished, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, teach us how to pray, the way John taught his own disciples."

L.1: And it happened, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying in a certain place, [that] when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples."

R.1: One time Jesus was praying in a certain place. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} finished, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, please teach us how to pray. John taught his disciples how to pray."

decisions.choice: praying: Luke shows Jesus at prayer before he teaches about prayer
decisions.reason: Luke often shows Jesus praying at turning points (3:21; 5:16; 6:12; 9:18, 28-29). Here the disciples see him pray and ask him to teach them.

decisions.choice: as John taught his disciples: a teacher gave his followers a way of praying of their own
decisions.reason: John's disciples were known for their prayers (5:33). A prayer given by a teacher marked out his followers as a group. The disciple asks Jesus for a prayer for those who follow him.

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect for Jesus as teacher and master
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite "sir", but a disciple uses it here of the one he follows, and Luke's readers hear in it the title of the risen Jesus (2:11).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: two sentences: the request, then John's example
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the request short and gives the comparison as its own sentence.

records.heading: Lord, teach us to pray

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· Πάτερ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·
records.gloss: He said then to them, When you pray, say, Father, let be hallowed the name of you; let come the kingdom of you;
pieces: He said to them, "When you pray, say: 'Father, may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be honored as holy. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come.

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "When you pray, say: 'Father, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be held holy; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come.

R.2: Jesus said to them, "When you pray, say this: 'Father, may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be treated as holy. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come.

decisions.choice: Father ... let your kingdom come: Luke's shorter form, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Our Father who is in heaven" and "let your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth", the reading of many later manuscripts
a prayer for the Holy Spirit to come and cleanse us, in place of the prayer for the kingdom, found in a very few manuscripts and early writers
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts fill out Luke's prayer with words from the longer form in Matthew 6:9-10: "our ... who is in heaven" after "Father", and a request that God's will be done on earth as in heaven. The oldest manuscripts, including the papyrus P75 and Codex Vaticanus, have the shorter form. Scribes were far more likely to make Luke match the better-known form in Matthew than to shorten it. A very few witnesses have a request for the Holy Spirit instead of the request for the kingdom. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Father: God addressed directly as Father
decisions.reason: Jesus himself prays to God as "Father" (10:21; 22:42; 23:34, 46), and he gives his disciples the same way of speaking to God. Luke has the one word, without the additions found in Matthew.

decisions.choice: let your name be held holy: may God be honored as the holy God he is
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known. The request is that his name be treated as holy by all people, and that God himself show his holiness, as he promised to do (Ezekiel 36:22-23). The passive form leaves both in view.

decisions.choice: let your kingdom come: may God's rule come in full
decisions.reason: Jesus proclaims the kingdom of God (4:43; 8:1) and sends his disciples to say it has come near (10:9, 11). The prayer asks God to bring his rule in its fullness.

decisions.choice: let ... be held holy (L); may ... be honored as holy (B); may ... be treated as holy (R)
decisions.reason: "Hallowed" is the familiar word in this prayer, but it is no longer used in everyday speech. Each level says what it means.

decisions.choice: the prayer is a quotation inside Jesus' words, in single quotation marks; it closes at the end of 11:4
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the words of the prayer inside his own speech.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.source: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν·
records.gloss: The bread of us the daily give to us each day;
pieces: Each day give us the bread we need.

L.3: Our daily bread give us each day;

R.3: Give us the food we need for each day.

decisions.choice: daily: the bread needed for the day
alternatives: for tomorrow, for the coming day
for the age to come, the bread of the kingdom
decisions.reason: The adjective (epiousios) is found almost nowhere outside this prayer (here and Matthew 6:11). In the third century Origen already said he knew it from no other Greek writing. It may be built from words meaning "the coming [day]" or from words meaning "being, existence". "Daily" goes back to the oldest Latin versions and fits the request "each day". Either way the prayer asks God for the food his people need, one day at a time.

decisions.choice: bread given each day: as God gave the manna day by day
alternatives: a store of food for the future
decisions.reason: In the wilderness God gave the manna each day, enough for that day (Exodus 16:4). Luke's "each day" and the present tense of "give" make it a request repeated day after day; Matthew 6:11 has "today".

decisions.choice: bread: food in general
decisions.reason: Bread was the main food of every meal, and the word often stands for food as a whole.

decisions.choice: Our daily bread first
alternatives: Give us each day our daily bread
decisions.reason: The Greek puts the bread first, for emphasis. Literal keeps that order.

decisions.choice: the bread we need (B); the food we need for each day (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what is asked for: what we need for the day. "Daily bread" is kept at Literal.

records.source: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.
records.gloss: and forgive us the sins of us, also for ourselves we forgive everyone being indebted to us; and not lead us into temptation.
pieces: Forgive us our sins, since we also forgive all who owe us. And do not bring us into temptation.'"

L.4: and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone owing us; and do not lead us into temptation.'"

R.4: Forgive us for our sins, because we forgive everyone who has done wrong to us. And keep us away from temptation.'"

decisions.choice: everyone owing us: everyone who has wronged us
alternatives: only those who owe us money
decisions.reason: A wrong done to someone is pictured as a debt owed to them, as in the story of the two debtors (7:41-47). Matthew 6:12 speaks of debts in both halves of the request; Luke has "sins" for what we owe God and keeps the picture of debt for what others owe us.

decisions.choice: for we ourselves also forgive: those who ask God's forgiveness forgive others
decisions.reason: The present tense describes a settled practice. Those who ask God to forgive them do not hold others' wrongs against them (6:37; 17:3-4). The prayer does not make our forgiving the price of God's; it shows what kind of people pray it.

decisions.choice: temptation: a testing that could lead to sin or falling away
decisions.reason: The word covers both being tempted to do wrong (4:13) and being tested by hardship or opposition (8:13; 22:28). Jesus tells the disciples to pray that they may not enter into it (22:40, 46). The request asks God to keep his people from such testing and from falling in it; God himself tempts no one to sin (James 1:13).

decisions.choice: the prayer ends with "into temptation", as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: "but deliver us from evil" added, as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the request "but rescue us from evil" from Matthew 6:13. The oldest manuscripts, including P75 and Codex Vaticanus, end the prayer here. The closing words of praise known from later use of Matthew's prayer are not found in any manuscript of Luke. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: all who owe us (B); everyone who has done wrong to us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of debt; Readable says what the debt stands for.

decisions.choice: keep us away from temptation
alternatives: do not lead us into temptation
decisions.reason: Readable puts the request in positive words: the one praying asks God not to bring them into temptation, that is, to keep them from it.

records.source: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους, ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·
records.gloss: And he said to them, Who of you will have a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves, \v 6 since a friend of me has come from a journey to me and nothing I have what I will set before him;
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Imagine that one of you has a friend, and you go to his house in the middle of the night and say to him, 'My friend, lend me three loaves.
Another friend of mine has come to my house from a journey, and I have nothing to set out for him to eat.'

L.5: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Which of you will have a friend, and will go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves,
L.6: since a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,'

R.5: Then Jesus said to them, "Suppose one of you goes to a friend's house in the middle of the night. You say to him, 'Friend, please lend me three loaves of bread.
R.6: A friend of mine has been traveling, and he has just come to stay with me. I do not have any food to give him.'

decisions.choice: which of you will have a friend ...: a question that runs on to 11:7 and expects the answer "none of you"
alternatives: a plain statement about one person
decisions.reason: The question begins here and runs through the sleeper's answer in 11:7. Jesus asks his hearers whether they can imagine a friend turning them away: no one would expect that. 11:8 then adds that even if friendship were not enough, the man would still get up.

decisions.choice: a guest at midnight: welcoming a traveler with food was a duty
alternatives: an ordinary request at a convenient time
decisions.reason: Travelers often went on through the evening. To welcome a guest and set food before him was a duty that Scripture honors (Genesis 18:1-8). Bread was usually baked each day, so by night a household might have none left.

decisions.choice: three loaves: small flat loaves, enough for a meal
decisions.reason: Loaves were small and round. Three would make a meal for a guest, with some to spare.

decisions.choice: Imagine that one of you (B); Suppose one of you (R)
alternatives: Which of you will have a friend ...?
decisions.reason: The Greek question is long and runs into 11:7. Balanced and Readable start it as a story the hearers are asked to picture.

decisions.choice: to my house (B); to stay with me (R); for him to eat (B)
decisions.reason: The friend has come to the man's home as a guest. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.heading: The friend at midnight

records.source: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.
records.gloss: and that one from within answering will say, Not me troubles cause; already the door has been shut, and the children of me with me in the bed are; not I am able having risen to give to you.
pieces: Would that friend call back from inside, 'Do not trouble me. The door is already shut for the night, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up now to hand you anything'?

L.7: and that one, answering from inside, will say, 'Do not cause me trouble; the door has already been shut, and my children are with me in bed; I am not able to get up and give [anything] to you'?

R.7: Would your friend answer from inside the house, 'Do not bother me! The door is already locked. My children are in bed with me. I cannot get out of bed to give you anything'?

decisions.choice: the door shut, the children in bed: the whole household is asleep
alternatives: a large house with many rooms
decisions.reason: In a small village house the family often slept together in one room. Getting up meant unbarring the door and waking the children.

decisions.choice: will answer: still part of the question begun in 11:5
decisions.reason: The sleeper's answer completes the question Jesus asked. The expected reply is that no friend would answer like this.

decisions.choice: a question: Would that friend ...? (B); Would your friend ...? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the question plain at the point where the answer comes, since the start of the question is now some way back.

decisions.choice: for the night
decisions.reason: The door is shut because the household has gone to bed.

records.source: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.
records.gloss: I say to you, if even not he will give to him having risen because of the being friend of him, because of yet the shamelessness of him having risen he will give him as much as he needs.
pieces: I tell you, even if friendship is not enough to get him out of bed to give you the bread, your boldness in asking without shame will get him up, and he will give you as much as you need.

L.8: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will get up and give him as much as he needs.

R.8: I tell you, being his friend may not be enough to make him get up and give you bread. But you were not ashamed to ask, even in the middle of the night. So he will get up and give you all you need.

decisions.choice: shamelessness: boldness that does not hold back for fear of shame
decisions.reason: The word means shamelessness, a lack of the restraint that shame would bring. Older renderings took it as persistence, but the man asks only once in the story. His boldness is in asking at all, at midnight, sure that his friend will help.

decisions.choice: his: the man who comes asking
alternatives: the man in bed, who gets up to avoid the shame of refusing a guest
decisions.reason: Several of the pronouns in this verse could refer to either man. Taken with 11:9-10, the point is the boldness of the one who asks. Some read it of the sleeper: he gets up so as not to be shamed for failing a neighbor's guest.

decisions.choice: the lesson: if a sleepy friend gives, God will surely give
alternatives: we must wear God down by asking
decisions.reason: The story argues from the lesser to the greater, as 11:13 does. God is not the reluctant friend; he is the one who gives far more readily.

decisions.choice: you, your (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of the asker in the third person. Balanced and Readable go on speaking to "you", as the story began in 11:5, so the reader can tell the two men apart.

records.source: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·
records.gloss: And I to you say, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
pieces: So I tell you: ask, and God will give to you; search, and you will find; knock, and God will open the door for you.

L.9: And I say to you, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

R.9: So I tell you, keep asking God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you what you ask for. Keep looking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and the door will be opened for you.

decisions.choice: it will be given, it will be opened: God is the giver
decisions.reason: The passive is a reverent way of speaking of what God does. 11:13 names the giver: the Father.

decisions.choice: ask, seek, knock: commands for a lasting practice
decisions.reason: The commands are in the present tense, which describes ongoing action: keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking.

decisions.choice: knock: ask to be let in, as the friend did at the door
alternatives: a call to force the door
decisions.reason: The picture follows the story of the friend at the door (11:5-8).

decisions.choice: God will give ... God will open the door (B); God, and he will give (R); the door (B, R)
alternatives: it will be given ... it will be opened
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the giver, which the passive implies, and name the door that is opened.

decisions.choice: keep asking ... keep looking ... keep knocking
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the ongoing sense of the commands.

records.heading: Ask, search, knock

records.source: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
records.gloss: Everyone for the asking receives, and the [one] seeking finds, and to the [one] knocking it will be opened.
pieces: For all who ask receive, all who search find, and all who knock have the door opened to them.

L.10: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

R.10: Everyone who asks will receive. Everyone who looks will find. And the door will be opened for everyone who knocks.

decisions.choice: for: the reason to ask
decisions.reason: The promise holds for everyone who asks, and that is why the disciples should ask.

decisions.choice: it will be opened: future, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: it is opened: present, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ between the future and the present tense here. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable gives each promise its own sentence.

decisions.choice: the door
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the door that is opened, as in 11:9.

records.source: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;
records.gloss: Which now of you the father will ask the son for a fish, and instead of a fish a snake to him will give?
pieces: Is there a father among you who would hand his son a snake when the boy asked for a fish?

L.11: And which father among you, [if his] son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?

R.11: You fathers, suppose your son asks you for a fish. Would you give him a snake instead?

decisions.choice: a fish ... a snake: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "bread ... a stone" first, then the fish and the snake, as in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add a first question, about a son asking for bread and being given a stone, from Matthew 7:9. Several early manuscripts lack it, and it is likely to have come in from Matthew. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "no"
decisions.reason: No father would do such a thing. Each pair puts something harmful in place of the food the child asked for.

decisions.choice: You fathers, suppose ... Would you ...?
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the question into two short sentences.

records.source: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;
records.gloss: Or also he will ask for an egg, will he give to him a scorpion?
pieces: Or if he asked for an egg, would he give him a scorpion?

L.12: Or also [if] he asks for an egg, will [he] give him a scorpion?

R.12: Or if he asks for an egg, would you give him a scorpion?

decisions.choice: scorpion: a small creature with a painful, poisonous sting
decisions.reason: Scorpions were common in the land and in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:15; Luke 10:19).

decisions.choice: would you give
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking to the fathers as "you", as in 11:11.

records.source: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: If therefore you evil being know gifts good to give to the children of you, how much more the Father the from heaven will give [the] Spirit Holy to those asking him.
pieces: You are evil, and yet you know how to give your children good gifts. Then how much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

L.13: If then you, being evil, know [how] to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give [the] Holy Spirit to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

R.13: Even though you are evil, you know how to give good things to your children. So the Father in heaven will be much more ready to give the Holy Spirit to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If human fathers, sinful as they are, give their children good things, God the Father will surely give his best gift.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, the oldest among them, read "the Holy Spirit". A few have "good things", the wording of Matthew 7:11, or similar phrases. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit: the gift the Father gives
decisions.reason: John promised that the one coming would baptize with the Holy Spirit (3:16). Jesus later promises the Spirit as the Father's gift (24:49; Acts 1:4-5; 2:33).

decisions.choice: the Father from heaven: the heavenly Father
alternatives: the Father will give from heaven
decisions.reason: The words "from heaven" can describe the Father, as "heavenly" does, or say where the gift comes from. Either way the giver is the Father in heaven.

decisions.choice: evil: sinful, compared with God's goodness
decisions.reason: Jesus is not singling out especially bad fathers. Compared with God, all people are sinful (18:19).

decisions.choice: a statement first, then the conclusion
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the fact about human fathers first, which makes the argument easier to follow.

records.source: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός.
records.gloss: And he was casting out a demon mute; it came about then the demon having gone out spoke the mute.
pieces: Jesus was driving out a demon that had left a man unable to speak. Once the demon was gone, the man spoke.

L.14: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was casting out a demon [that was] mute; and it happened, when the demon had gone out, the mute [man] spoke.

R.14: Jesus was forcing a demon to come out of a man. The demon had made the man unable to talk. When the demon came out, the man began to speak.

decisions.choice: a mute demon: a demon that made the man unable to speak
alternatives: a demon that could not speak
decisions.reason: The demon is named by what it did to the man. The word can mean deaf as well as mute (7:22); here the man speaks once he is free.

decisions.choice: Jesus; a man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section and say that the demon was in a man.

records.heading: By the finger of God

records.source: καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·
records.gloss: And marveled the crowds.
pieces: The crowds were amazed.

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people" for the crowds who watched.

records.source: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·
records.gloss: Some then of them said, By Beelzebul the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons;
pieces: But some of them said, "It is by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drives out the demons."

L.15: But some of them said, "By Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} casts out the demons."

R.15: But some of the people said, "Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, gives {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} power to force demons out."

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons: a name for Satan
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the charge by speaking of Satan (11:18), so the name stands for him. It recalls Baal-zebub, a god of the Philistine city of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2-3), a name that means "lord of flies". The form "zebul" may mean a lofty house, which would fit the pictures of the kingdom and the house in 11:17-22.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Beelzebub, the reading of the old Latin and Syriac versions
Beezebul, the reading of a few early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Greek manuscripts mostly read Beelzebul; a few early ones have Beezebul. The form Beelzebub, familiar from older translations, comes from the ancient versions and matches the name in 2 Kings 1:2. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by: by the power of
decisions.reason: They do not deny that the demon has gone. They claim that the power behind Jesus is Satan's.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul ... gives him power to force demons out
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "by Beelzebul" means.

records.source: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Others then testing a sign from heaven were seeking from him.
pieces: Others, wanting to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a sign from heaven.

L.16: And others, testing [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], were seeking from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a sign from heaven.

R.16: Others wanted to test Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show them a sign from heaven to prove that God had sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: sign: a visible act from God that would prove Jesus' claims
decisions.reason: They had just seen a demon driven out, yet they ask for more: a proof from heaven that could not be doubted. Jesus answers in 11:29-30.

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: Heaven stands for God. They want a sign that God himself gives, though some may have pictured a wonder in the sky.

decisions.choice: testing: putting him to the test, hoping to trap him
decisions.reason: The word is used of the devil's testing (4:2, 12) and of the expert in the law who tested Jesus (10:25).

decisions.choice: to prove that God had sent him
decisions.reason: Readable says what such a sign from heaven was meant to show.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.source: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.
records.gloss: He now knowing of them the thoughts said to them, Every kingdom against itself having been divided is laid waste, and house against house falls.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew what they were thinking, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "If a kingdom is torn apart by its own people, it is laid waste, and its houses fall one upon another.

L.17: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, knowing their thoughts, said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.

R.17: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "If the people of a kingdom fight against each other, that kingdom will be destroyed. Its houses will fall down on top of each other.

decisions.choice: house falls upon house: in the ruin of a divided kingdom, houses collapse on one another
alternatives: a household divided against itself falls
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and can be read two ways. It may go on picturing the kingdom laid waste, its houses falling in heaps. Or it may be a second example, a divided household that falls, as in Mark 3:25 and Matthew 12:25.

decisions.choice: knowing their thoughts: Jesus knows what they think
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing people's thoughts (5:22; 6:8; 9:47).

decisions.choice: is laid waste: is brought to ruin
decisions.reason: The word is used of a land or city left in ruins.

decisions.choice: torn apart by its own people (B); the people of a kingdom fight against each other (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for a kingdom to be divided against itself.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.source: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: If now also the Satan against himself was divided, how will stand the kingdom of him?
pieces: If Satan too is split against himself, how can his kingdom last?

L.18: And if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand?

R.18: In the same way, if Satan is fighting against himself, how can his kingdom last?

decisions.choice: Satan: the enemy of God and his people, the devil
decisions.reason: Satan is the devil who tested Jesus (4:1-13). Jesus treats Beelzebul (11:15) as another name for him.

decisions.choice: how will his kingdom stand: a question expecting the answer that it cannot
decisions.reason: If Satan were driving out his own demons he would be destroying his own rule. The charge makes no sense.

decisions.choice: In the same way
decisions.reason: Readable shows how Satan's case follows from the picture of the kingdom in 11:17.

records.source: ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.
records.gloss: For you say by Beelzebul cast out I the demons.
pieces: Yet that is what you are saying: that I drive out the demons by Beelzebul.

L.18: For you say that I cast out the demons by Beelzebul.

R.18: And yet you say that Beelzebul gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} power to force demons out.

decisions.choice: for: why Jesus speaks of Satan divided against himself
decisions.reason: Jesus explains why he has raised the question: their charge would mean that Satan is fighting himself.

decisions.choice: Yet that is what you are saying (B); And yet you say (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the link with the question before it.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν;
records.gloss: If now I by Beelzebul cast out the demons, the sons of you by whom do they cast out?
pieces: And if I drive out the demons by Beelzebul, by whose power do your own people drive them out?

L.19: And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast [them] out?

R.19: If Beelzebul gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} power to force demons out, then who gives your own followers power to force them out?

decisions.choice: your sons: your own followers, people of your own group
decisions.reason: "Sons" can mean followers or members of a group. Some Jews of the time also drove out demons (compare Acts 19:13-14). If Jesus' power came from Satan, so would theirs.

decisions.choice: if I cast out ... by Beelzebul: supposed for the sake of argument
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up their claim to show where it leads.

decisions.choice: your own people (B); your own followers (R)
decisions.reason: "Your sons" would suggest their children. Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.
records.gloss: Because of this they of you judges will be.
pieces: So they themselves will be the ones to judge you.

L.19: Because of this they will be your judges.

R.19: So your own followers will show that you are wrong.

decisions.choice: they will be your judges: their own work shows the charge to be false
alternatives: they will judge you on the last day
decisions.reason: The work of their own people shows that driving out demons is not Satan's work, so it judges the accusers. Some also see a reference to the final judgment.

decisions.choice: will show that you are wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what this judging consists of here.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: If however by [the] finger of God I cast out the demons, then has come upon you the kingdom of God.
pieces: But suppose it is by God's finger that I drive the demons out. Then the kingdom of God has already reached you.

L.20: But if I cast out the demons by [the] finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

R.20: But suppose I force demons out by the finger of God, that is, by God's own power. Then the kingdom of God has already come to you.

decisions.choice: the finger of God: Exodus 8:19
alternatives: a figure of speech with no background
decisions.reason: When the magicians of Egypt could not match the plague of gnats, they told Pharaoh that it was the finger of God. The tablets of the law were written by the finger of God (Exodus 31:18). Jesus' power over demons is the same power God showed at the exodus. Matthew 12:28 has "the Spirit of God".

decisions.choice: has come upon you: has arrived, has reached you
decisions.reason: The verb means to arrive or reach. God's rule is already present in Jesus' work of setting people free.

decisions.choice: if: a condition Jesus means as true
decisions.reason: This is the real explanation of his power, set against the false one in 11:19.

decisions.choice: suppose ... Then ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the condition into two sentences.

decisions.choice: that is, by God's own power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's finger.

records.source: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: When the strong [man] being fully armed guards the his own courtyard, in peace are the possessions of him;
pieces: As long as a strong man keeps guard over his own palace with all his weapons, his goods are left in peace.

L.21: When the strong [man], fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are in peace.

R.21: When a strong man guards his own house with all his weapons, his things are left in peace.

decisions.choice: in peace: safe and undisturbed
decisions.reason: The word here means safety: no one touches his goods.

decisions.choice: courtyard: a house built around a courtyard, a palace
decisions.reason: The word first meant a courtyard, then a large house or palace built around one.

decisions.choice: the strong man: Satan, who holds people in his power
decisions.reason: The picture explains the driving out of demons. Satan guards what he holds, but a stronger one has come (11:22).

decisions.choice: palace (B); house (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the building the courtyard belongs to.

records.source: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.
records.gloss: when however one stronger than he having come upon [him] overcomes him, the full armor of him he takes away in which he had trusted, and the spoils of him he divides.
pieces: But then a man stronger than he is comes against him and wins the fight. He strips away all the armor the strong man was counting on, and shares out the goods he has seized.

L.22: but when one stronger than he comes upon [him and] overcomes him, he takes away his full armor in which he had trusted, and divides his spoils.

R.22: But then someone stronger comes and attacks him and beats him. He takes away all the weapons and armor the strong man trusted. Then he gives away the things he took from him.

decisions.choice: one stronger: Jesus, the stronger one John promised
decisions.reason: John said that one stronger than he would come (3:16), using the same word. Jesus' power over the demons shows that he has overcome Satan.

decisions.choice: divides his spoils: Isaiah 49:24-25; 53:12
decisions.reason: Isaiah asks whether the prey can be taken from the mighty, and the LORD answers that it will be. The LORD's servant divides the spoil with the strong. The people Satan held are set free.

decisions.choice: full armor: all his weapons and armor
decisions.reason: The word means a soldier's full equipment for battle.

decisions.choice: two or three sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the struggle step by step, and name "the strong man" so the reader can tell the two apart.

records.source: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
records.gloss: The [one] not being with me against me is, and the [one] not gathering with me scatters.
pieces: Anyone who does not stand with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stands against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and anyone who does not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gather is scattering.

L.23: The one who is not with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who does not gather with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} scatters.

R.23: If you are not with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you are against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If you do not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gather, you are scattering.

decisions.choice: gather, scatter: a picture of gathering a flock
decisions.reason: God promised to gather his scattered flock (Ezekiel 34:12-13). Jesus is gathering God's people; whoever does not join in works against it.

decisions.choice: no neutral ground
decisions.reason: In 9:50 Jesus told the disciples not to stop a man who drove out demons in his name: whoever is not against them is for them. Here he speaks of each person's own stand toward him. The two sayings answer different situations.

decisions.choice: If you ...
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly.

records.source: Ὅταν τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ μὴ εὑρίσκον λέγει· Ὑποστρέψω εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον·
records.gloss: When the unclean spirit goes out from the man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding it says, I will return to the house of me from where I came out;
pieces: When an unclean spirit has left a {{gender:person|man}}, it wanders through dry, empty places looking for a place to rest. When it finds none, it says, 'I will go back to my house, where I came from.'

L.24: When the unclean spirit has gone out from the {{gender:person|man}}, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding [any], it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.'

R.24: When an evil spirit comes out of someone, it travels through the desert looking for a place to rest. But it does not find one. So it says, 'I will go back to the house I came from.'

decisions.choice: unclean spirit: an evil spirit, a demon
alternatives: a spirit that is physically dirty
decisions.reason: Luke uses "unclean spirit" and "demon" for the same beings (4:33; 8:27-29).

decisions.choice: waterless places: the desert, thought of as a haunt of evil spirits
decisions.reason: The desert was pictured as the home of wild creatures and spirits (Isaiah 34:14; Luke 8:29).

decisions.choice: my house: the person the spirit had lived in
decisions.reason: The spirit speaks of the person it left as its home.

decisions.choice: evil spirit (R); unclean spirit (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Unclean" here means evil, not dirty. Readable says "evil", as in 4:33.

decisions.choice: person as the default, man as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, man or woman. Readable says "someone".

records.heading: The unclean spirit returns

records.source: καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
records.gloss: And having come it finds swept and put in order.
pieces: It arrives and finds the house swept and tidied.

L.25: And having come, it finds [it] swept and put in order.

R.25: When it gets there, it finds that the house has been swept clean and everything is neat.

decisions.choice: it finds it swept: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: it finds it empty, swept, as in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "empty" from Matthew 12:44. Most early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: swept and put in order: cleaned up, but with no one living there
decisions.reason: The person has been set free, but nothing has taken the spirit's place. 11:28 says what should fill the life: hearing God's word and keeping it.

decisions.choice: the house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the house, to make clear what is found swept.

records.source: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτά, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ, καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
records.gloss: Then it goes and takes other spirits more evil than itself seven, and having entered they dwell there, and becomes the last of the man that worse than the first.
pieces: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and make their home there. In the end that {{gender:person|man}} is worse off than at the start."

L.26: Then it goes and takes along seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having gone in they settle there; and the last [state] of that {{gender:person|man}} becomes worse than the first."

R.26: Then it goes and gets seven other spirits that are even more evil than it is. They all go into the person and live there. So in the end that person is worse off than before."

decisions.choice: seven: a full number
decisions.reason: Seven stands for completeness. The person is now wholly in the power of evil (compare the seven demons of 8:2).

decisions.choice: worse than the first: being set free from evil is not enough
alternatives: a story about one case only
decisions.reason: The warning follows 11:23: a life emptied of evil but not given to Jesus is open to worse.

decisions.choice: the last [things]: the final condition
decisions.reason: The plural means the state the person ends up in, compared with the state at the start.

decisions.choice: person as the default, man as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:24. Readable says "that person".

decisions.choice: is worse off than at the start (B); than before (R)
alternatives: the last state is worse than the first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·
records.gloss: It came about then in the saying him these things, having lifted up a certain voice a woman from the crowd said to him, Blessed the womb having borne you and breasts that you nursed.
pieces: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed is the woman who carried {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in her womb and fed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at her breasts!"

L.27: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying these things, a certain woman from the crowd, raising [her] voice, said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed [is] the womb that bore {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and the breasts {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} nursed from!"

R.27: While Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd shouted to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How blessed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mother is! She carried {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} inside her body and fed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at her breast!"

decisions.choice: the womb and the breasts: a way of praising a son by praising his mother
decisions.reason: To call the mother blessed is to praise the son she bore. The woman honors Jesus through his mother.

decisions.choice: blessed: happy, favored by God
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Mary in 1:45, and Mary said that all generations would call her blessed (1:48).

decisions.choice: the woman who carried you in her womb (B); your mother (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the mother the woman is praising.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.heading: Hearing and keeping God's word

records.source: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.
records.gloss: He then said, Rather blessed those hearing the word of God and keeping.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Even more blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it."

L.28: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Rather, blessed [are] those who hear the word of God and keep [it]."

R.28: But Jesus answered, "Yes, but the people who hear the word of God and obey it are even more blessed."

decisions.choice: rather: yes, but even more
decisions.reason: The word can correct what was said or add to it. Luke has already shown Mary as blessed (1:42, 45, 48), so Jesus does not deny the woman's words. He points to what matters more: hearing and keeping God's word, as Mary herself did (1:38; 2:19, 51; 8:21).

decisions.choice: keep: obey and hold on to
decisions.reason: To keep God's word is to treasure it and live by it (8:15).

decisions.choice: obey it
decisions.reason: Readable says what keeping the word means.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.source: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ.
records.gloss: Of the now crowds pressing together he began to say, The generation this generation evil is; a sign it seeks, and a sign not will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
pieces: With the crowds pressing in more and more, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say, "This generation is an evil one. It looks for a sign, yet the only sign it will be given is the sign of Jonah.

L.29: And as the crowds were gathering together, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say, "This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah.

R.29: More and more people were crowding around Jesus. He said, "The people living today are evil. They want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to give them a sign. But the only sign they will get is the sign of Jonah.

decisions.choice: generation: the people of this time
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the people of his day as a whole, as in 7:31 and 9:41.

decisions.choice: sign: the proof from heaven they demanded
decisions.reason: This answers those who asked for a sign from heaven (11:16).

decisions.choice: the sign of Jonah: Jonah and his message to Nineveh
alternatives: a new wonder like the great fish
decisions.reason: 11:30 and 11:32 explain it: Jonah came to Nineveh with God's warning, and the city turned from its sin (Jonah 3).

decisions.choice: the crowds pressing together: the crowds growing larger
decisions.reason: The verb pictures crowds thronging together in greater numbers.

decisions.choice: The people living today
decisions.reason: Readable says who "this generation" is.

decisions.choice: They want me to give them a sign
decisions.reason: Readable names who is being asked for a sign.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.heading: Something greater than Jonah

records.source: καθὼς γὰρ ἐγένετο Ἰωνᾶς τοῖς Νινευίταις σημεῖον, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.
records.gloss: Just as for became Jonah to the Ninevites a sign, so will be also the Son of the Man to the generation this.
pieces: For just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

L.30: For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.

R.30: Jonah was a sign to the people who lived in the city of Nineveh. In the same way, the Son of Man will be a sign to the people living today.

decisions.choice: how Jonah was a sign: he came to Nineveh as one rescued by God, with God's warning
alternatives: only his time in the great fish
decisions.reason: God brought Jonah up alive from the sea and sent him to preach to Nineveh (Jonah 2-3). Matthew 12:40 draws out the three days in the fish; Luke puts the weight on Jonah's preaching (11:32).

decisions.choice: will be: pointing to what is still to come
decisions.reason: The future may point to Jesus' rising from the dead, or to the Son of Man's coming as judge, which the next verses speak of. Either way, God will give no other sign than the Son of Man himself.

decisions.choice: Ninevites: the people of Nineveh, capital of Assyria
decisions.reason: Nineveh was the great city of Assyria, Israel's enemy (Jonah 1:2; 3:3).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: As in 5:24 and 9:22.

decisions.choice: a sign (repeated)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "a sign", which the Greek leaves understood.

records.source: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτούς· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
records.gloss: The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of the generation this and will condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, greater than Solomon here.
pieces: At the judgment the queen of the South will stand up with the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the far ends of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom; and here is something greater than Solomon.

L.31: [The] queen of [the] South will rise up in the judgment with the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, [something] greater than Solomon [is] here.

R.31: On the day of judgment, the queen from the south will stand up with the {{gender:people|men}} living today and show that they are guilty. She came from a land very far away to listen to Solomon's wise teaching. And something greater than Solomon is right here!

decisions.choice: the queen of the South: the queen of Sheba, 1 Kings 10:1-13
decisions.reason: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's wisdom and came from far away to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1-13; 2 Chronicles 9:1-12). Sheba lay far to the south of Israel.

decisions.choice: will rise up in the judgment: will stand up at God's final judgment, as a witness
alternatives: will be raised from the dead at the judgment
decisions.reason: The words picture a court, where a witness stands up to speak. Her coming to hear Solomon will show up the people who will not listen to Jesus. The verb is also used of rising from the dead, and both may be in view.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "someone" but "something": what is happening in his words and work, God's kingdom coming. That includes Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: the men of this generation: the people of this time
decisions.reason: The word usually means men, but here it stands for the whole generation, as in 11:32. Some see a contrast: a woman from far away listened, while those here do not.

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The whole generation is meant, men and women.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: show that they are guilty
decisions.reason: Readable says what condemning means here: her example proves them guilty.

records.source: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
records.gloss: Men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with the generation this and will condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, greater than Jonah here.
pieces: At the judgment the {{gender:people|men}} of Nineveh will stand up with this generation and condemn it, because they repented when Jonah preached; and here is something greater than Jonah.

L.32: [The] {{gender:people|men}} of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and look, [something] greater than Jonah [is] here.

R.32: On the day of judgment, the {{gender:people|men}} of Nineveh will also stand up with the people living today and show that they are guilty. The people of Nineveh turned away from their sins when Jonah preached to them. And something greater than Jonah is right here!

decisions.choice: they repented at the preaching of Jonah: Jonah 3:5-10
decisions.reason: When Jonah preached, the people of Nineveh believed God, fasted and turned from their evil ways, and God spared the city.

decisions.choice: repented: turned from their wrong ways to God
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of heart and life (3:3, 8).

decisions.choice: will stand up in the judgment: will rise as witnesses at God's judgment
decisions.reason: As in 11:31.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter
decisions.reason: As in 11:31.

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The whole city repented, men and women (Jonah 3:5).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: turned away from their sins (R); repented (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means.

records.source: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φέγγος βλέπωσιν.
records.gloss: No one a lamp having lit into a hidden place puts nor under the basket but on the lampstand, that those entering the light may see.
pieces: A lamp, once lit, is not hidden away in a cellar or put under a basket; it is set on a lampstand, where anyone coming in will see its light.

L.33: No one, having lit a lamp, puts [it] in a hidden place or under the basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.

R.33: When someone lights a lamp, it is not hidden or put under a basket. It is put on a lampstand, so that people who come into the house can see by its light.

decisions.choice: or under the basket: included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, as in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, including the papyri P45 and P75, lack "or under the basket". The words may have come in from Matthew 5:15 and Mark 4:21, or been lost by accident. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a hidden place: a cellar or a hidden corner
decisions.reason: The word can mean a cellar or vault, a place out of sight.

decisions.choice: the basket: a container used to measure grain
decisions.reason: The word names a measure for grain, holding about two gallons, and the container used for it.

decisions.choice: the lamp: God's light, plainly shown
alternatives: a saying unrelated to what comes before
decisions.reason: Jesus used the picture in 8:16. Here it follows the demand for a sign: God has not hidden his light. The question is whether people see it (11:34-36).

decisions.choice: the lamp as subject, in the passive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the lamp the subject, which reads easily and avoids a vague "they".

records.heading: Light within

records.source: ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου.
records.gloss: The lamp of the body is the eye of you.
pieces: Your body's lamp is your eye.

L.34: The lamp of the body is your eye.

R.34: Your eye is like a lamp for your body.

decisions.choice: the lamp of the body: the eye lets light into the whole body
decisions.reason: The eye is pictured as the opening through which light reaches the whole person.

decisions.choice: like a lamp
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison plain.

records.source: ὅταν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινόν ἐστιν· ἐπὰν δὲ πονηρὸς ᾖ, καὶ τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινόν.
records.gloss: When the eye of you clear is, also all the body of you full of light is; when however evil it is, also the body of you dark.
pieces: If your eye is clear, light fills your whole body as well. If your eye is bad, darkness fills your body too.

L.34: When your eye is sound, your whole body also is full of light; but when it is evil, your body also [is] dark.

R.34: If your eye is healthy, light fills your whole body. But if your eye is bad, your body is in darkness.

decisions.choice: sound: healthy and clear; also single-minded and generous
decisions.reason: The word means simple, single, without a fold. Used of an eye, it means healthy. It is also used of a sincere, generous heart (Romans 12:8, "generously"). Both senses may be heard here.

decisions.choice: evil: diseased; also the "evil eye" of a grudging heart
decisions.reason: A bad eye cannot see. In Scripture an evil eye is also a picture of a mean or envious heart (Deuteronomy 15:9; Proverbs 28:22).

decisions.choice: the eye: the way a person takes in God's light
decisions.reason: The saying follows the demand for a sign. The light is there (11:33); the trouble is an eye that will not take it in.

decisions.choice: sound ... evil (L); clear ... bad (B); healthy ... bad (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses words that suit an eye; the decisions above give the other senses.

records.source: σκόπει οὖν μὴ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν.
records.gloss: Watch therefore lest the light that in you darkness is.
pieces: So be careful that the light inside you is not really darkness.

L.35: Watch out, then, lest the light that [is] in you is darkness.

R.35: So be careful. Do not let the light inside you turn out to be darkness.

decisions.choice: lest: a warning that it may already be so
decisions.reason: The form can express a fear that something is in fact the case: check whether what you take for light is really darkness.

decisions.choice: really (B); turn out to be (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of the warning.

records.source: εἰ οὖν τὸ σῶμά σου ὅλον φωτεινόν, μὴ ἔχον μέρος τι σκοτεινόν, ἔσται φωτεινὸν ὅλον ὡς ὅταν ὁ λύχνος τῇ ἀστραπῇ φωτίζῃ σε.
records.gloss: If therefore the body of you full of light, not having part any dark, will be full of light wholly as when the lamp with the brightness may light you.
pieces: So if light fills your whole body and no part of it is dark, it will be bright all through, as when a lamp shines on you with its beam."

L.36: If then your whole body [is] full of light, not having any part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp lights you with [its] brightness."

R.36: If your whole body is full of light, with no dark part at all, then you will be full of light. It will be like having a bright lamp shining on you."

decisions.choice: it will be wholly full of light: the result of having no dark part
alternatives: a simple repetition of the first half
decisions.reason: The second half seems to repeat the first. The weight falls on "wholly" and on the comparison: a life with no part kept back from God's light will shine all through, like someone in a lamp's full light. Some take the future to point to the last day.

decisions.choice: brightness: a flash or gleam of light
decisions.reason: The word is used of lightning (10:18; 17:24), and here of a lamp's bright light.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable gives the comparison its own sentence.

records.source: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.
records.gloss: In then the speaking, asks him a Pharisee that he would dine with him; having entered then he reclined.
pieces: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} finished speaking, a Pharisee asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to eat at his home, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went in and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.

L.37: Now as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke, a Pharisee asks {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to dine with him; and having gone in, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table].

R.37: When Jesus finished talking, a Pharisee asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come and eat at his house. So Jesus went in and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.

decisions.choice: Pharisee: one of a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 6:2. Pharisees kept the law strictly, together with the traditions about how to keep it, including rules about washing (Mark 7:3-4).

decisions.choice: as he spoke: as he finished, or just after
decisions.reason: The form can mean while he was speaking or when he had spoken. The invitation comes straight after the sayings of 11:29-36.

decisions.choice: dine: the word for an early or midday meal
decisions.reason: The word usually means the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning or around noon (compare 14:12).

decisions.choice: reclined: lay on a couch at the table, as guests did at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on couches around a low table, leaning on the left elbow (7:36-38).

decisions.choice: took his place at the table
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the meal in words a modern reader knows; the decision on "reclined" explains the custom.

decisions.choice: asked (past tense)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the present tense to tell the story vividly. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.heading: The inside of the cup

records.source: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν ὅτι οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.
records.gloss: And the Pharisee having seen marveled that not first he washed before the dinner.
pieces: The Pharisee saw that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not washed before the meal, and it surprised him.

L.38: And the Pharisee, seeing [it], was amazed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not first wash before the meal.

R.38: The Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} before the meal, as their custom required.

decisions.choice: wash: a washing for religious purity before eating
decisions.reason: The verb is the word for baptizing, to dip or wash. Many Jews, the Pharisees especially, washed before eating to be clean before God, by a tradition handed down from the elders (Mark 7:3-4). The law of Moses did not require it of ordinary people.

decisions.choice: having seen: he noticed and wondered
decisions.reason: Luke does not say the Pharisee said anything; Jesus answers what he saw in him.

decisions.choice: as their custom required
decisions.reason: Readable says why the Pharisee expected Jesus to wash.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.
records.gloss: Said then the Lord to him, Now you the Pharisees the outside of the cup and of the dish you cleanse, the and inside of you is full of plunder and wickedness.
pieces: But the Lord said to him, "You Pharisees clean the cup and the dish on the outside, but your own insides are full of plunder and wickedness.

L.39: But the Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.

R.39: Then the Lord said to him, "You Pharisees wash the outside of your cups and dishes. But inside, you are full of greed for what belongs to others, and full of evil.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke's name for Jesus in the story
decisions.reason: Luke the narrator often calls Jesus "the Lord" (7:13, 19; 10:1).

decisions.choice: cleanse the outside of the cup: rules for keeping vessels ritually clean
decisions.reason: The law gave rules for vessels that had become unclean (Leviticus 11:32-33), and tradition added more (Mark 7:4). Jesus uses the practice as a picture.

decisions.choice: plunder: robbery, grasping greed
decisions.reason: The word means taking things by force, and the greed behind it.

decisions.choice: your inside: you yourselves, within
decisions.reason: The picture turns from the cup to the people: their hearts are full of greed.

decisions.choice: greed for what belongs to others, and full of evil
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word for plunder.

records.source: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;
records.gloss: Fools, not the one having made the outside also the inside made?
pieces: Foolish people! The one who made the outside made the inside as well, did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?

L.40: Fools, did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?

R.40: You foolish people! God made the outside, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the inside too.

decisions.choice: the one who made: God, the maker of all
alternatives: the person who makes the cup
decisions.reason: Most likely Jesus means God, who made both the outside and the inside of a person and cares about both. Some take it of the potter who makes both sides of a cup; the point is the same.

decisions.choice: fools: people without sense
decisions.reason: In Scripture a fool is someone who does not reckon with God (12:20; Psalm 14:1).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the maker.

decisions.choice: a statement with a question at the end (B); a statement (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer "yes". Balanced and Readable state it.

records.source: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
records.gloss: But the things being within give alms, and behold, all things clean to you are.
pieces: Rather, give what is inside as gifts to the poor, and then everything is clean for you.

L.41: But give as alms the things inside, and look, all things are clean for you.

R.41: Instead, give what is inside your cups and dishes to poor people. Then everything will be clean for you.

decisions.choice: the things inside: what is in the cups and dishes
alternatives: as for what is inside you, give to the poor
decisions.reason: The words can mean the contents of the cups and dishes: give that food and wealth away. They can also mean "as for what is inside", turning to the heart. Either way, generosity cleanses where washing cannot.

decisions.choice: give alms: give gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of Jewish piety (12:33; Acts 10:2).

decisions.choice: all things are clean for you: generosity, not washing, makes clean
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the Pharisee's surprise at his not washing (11:38). A heart that gives is clean, and so is what it touches.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: inside your cups and dishes
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading in the first decision.

records.source: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.
records.gloss: But woe to you the Pharisees, for you tithe the mint and the rue and every herb, and pass by the justice and the love of God; these things but it was necessary to do and those not to neglect.
pieces: But how terrible for you Pharisees! You set aside for God a tenth even of mint and rue and every kind of garden plant, yet you pass over justice and the love of God. Justice and love are what you should have practiced, while not neglecting the tenth.

L.42: But woe to you Pharisees, for you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God; but these you ought to have done, and not neglected those.

R.42: How terrible for you Pharisees! You give one tenth of everything to God, even of the little plants you grow for flavor, like mint and rue. But you do not care about justice or about loving God. You should do these things, and keep giving a tenth as well.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over people facing God's judgment
decisions.reason: The prophets used the cry over those who would not turn back (Isaiah 5:8-22; Habakkuk 2:6-19). It is a lament and a warning, not a wish for harm. Jesus used it in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: tithe: give a tenth to God
decisions.reason: The law required a tenth of grain, wine, oil and produce to be given to God (Leviticus 27:30; Deuteronomy 14:22-23). The Pharisees counted even the smallest garden herbs.

decisions.choice: mint and rue: small garden herbs
decisions.reason: Mint and rue were used for flavor and medicine. Later Jewish teaching counted rue among the plants that did not need to be tithed (Mishnah, Shebiith 9:1), so tithing it went beyond what was required.

decisions.choice: justice: doing right by others
decisions.reason: The word can mean judgment, but here it means fairness and right dealing, as the prophets demanded (Micah 6:8).

decisions.choice: the love of God: love for God
decisions.reason: Most likely the love people owe to God (Deuteronomy 6:5; Luke 10:27). Jesus sets it beside justice: love for God and right dealing with others.

decisions.choice: the last sentence included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sentence missing, as in one ancient manuscript
decisions.reason: One ancient manuscript, Codex Bezae, lacks the closing words "these you ought to have done". Nearly all others have them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is rarely heard in everyday speech. Literal keeps the old cry; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as in the woes of 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: Justice and love ... the tenth (B); these things ... giving a tenth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "these" and "those" refer to.

decisions.choice: the little plants you grow for flavor
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of plants these are.

records.heading: How terrible for you

records.source: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.
records.gloss: Woe to you the Pharisees, for you love the first seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
pieces: How terrible for you Pharisees! You love to sit in the front seats of the synagogues and to be greeted in the marketplaces.

L.43: Woe to you Pharisees, for you love the front seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.

R.43: How terrible for you Pharisees! You love to sit in the seats of honor in the synagogues. And you love it when people greet you with respect in the markets.

decisions.choice: the front seat: the seats of honor at the front of the synagogue
decisions.reason: The places of honor were at the front, in view of the people (20:46).

decisions.choice: greetings: public greetings of respect, with titles of honor
decisions.reason: In the busy marketplaces, respected teachers were greeted with honor (20:46).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

records.source: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.
records.gloss: Woe to you, for you are like the graves the unmarked, and the men walking over not know.
pieces: How terrible for you! You are like graves with no marker, and the {{gender:people|men}} who walk over them are unaware of it."

L.44: Woe to you, for you are like unmarked graves, and the {{gender:people|men}} who walk over [them] do not know [it]."

R.44: How terrible for you! You are like graves that have no marker. People walk over them without knowing that they are there, and so they become unclean."

decisions.choice: unmarked graves: touching a grave made a person unclean
decisions.reason: Anyone who touched a grave was unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:16). Graves were marked so that people could keep away from them. Walking over an unmarked grave made a person unclean without knowing it.

decisions.choice: the point: people are made unclean by the Pharisees without knowing it
alternatives: the Pharisees are dead inside only
decisions.reason: The Pharisees, so careful about cleanness, spread uncleanness to those who follow them.

decisions.choice: Woe to you: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites", as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites", the wording of Matthew 23:27. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: and so they become unclean
decisions.reason: Readable says why walking over a grave mattered, from the first decision.

records.source: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.
records.gloss: Answering now one of the lawyers says to him, Teacher, these things saying also us you insult.
pieces: One of the experts in the law responded to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, by saying this {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are insulting us as well."

L.45: And answering, one of the experts in the law says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, by saying these things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} insult us also."

R.45: One of the experts in God's law said to Jesus, "Teacher, what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are saying insults us too!"

decisions.choice: experts in the law: men trained in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: As in 7:30 and 10:25. They taught and applied God's law. Many were Pharisees, so Jesus' words about the Pharisees struck them too.

decisions.choice: insult: treat with contempt, put to shame
decisions.reason: The word means to mistreat or shame someone.

decisions.choice: experts in God's law (R); experts in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts. The word means someone expert in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: says (L); responded, said (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek tells the story in the present tense. Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.heading: Loads too heavy to carry

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.
records.gloss: And he said, Also to you the lawyers woe, for you burden the men burdens heavy to bear, and yourselves with one of the fingers of you not do touch the burdens.
pieces: He said, "How terrible for you experts in the law too! You pile on {{gender:people|men}} loads that are hard to carry, and you yourselves will not touch those loads with even one of your fingers.

L.46: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Woe to you experts in the law also, for you load {{gender:people|men}} with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.

R.46: Jesus answered, "How terrible for you experts in God's law too! You make people carry heavy loads of rules. But you yourselves will not even put one finger on those loads to help them.

decisions.choice: burdens hard to carry: demands about keeping the law that weigh people down
decisions.reason: The experts laid on people rules about how to keep the law. Peter later speaks of a yoke too heavy to bear (Acts 15:10).

decisions.choice: do not touch the burdens with a finger: do nothing to help carry them
alternatives: do not keep the rules themselves
decisions.reason: Most likely they give no help to those who struggle under the load. Some take it to mean that they find ways round the rules for themselves.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: of rules; to help them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loads are and why they should touch them.

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

records.source: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets, the and fathers of you killed them.
