pieces: How terrible for you! You build monuments over the prophets' graves, yet those prophets died at the hands of your ancestors.

L.47: Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

R.47: How terrible for you! You build tombs to honor the prophets. But your own ancestors were the ones who killed those prophets.

decisions.choice: build the tombs of the prophets: put up monuments to honor them
decisions.reason: The prophets had died long before. Building fine tombs over their graves was a way of honoring them.

decisions.choice: fathers: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in 6:23, 26. Israel had often rejected and killed its prophets (1 Kings 19:10; Jeremiah 26:20-23; Luke 13:34).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" would suggest their parents.

decisions.choice: monuments over the prophets' graves (B); tombs to honor the prophets (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the building was for.

records.source: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.
records.gloss: So witnesses you are and consent to the works of the fathers of you, for they indeed killed them, you now build.
pieces: So you are witnesses, and you give your approval to what your ancestors did: they did the killing, and you do the building.

L.48: So you are witnesses and approve of the works of your fathers, for they killed them, and you build [their tombs].

R.48: So you show that you agree with what your ancestors did. Your ancestors killed the prophets, and you build tombs for them.

decisions.choice: witnesses who approve: by building the tombs they finish what their ancestors began
alternatives: they honor the prophets and so condemn their ancestors
decisions.reason: Jesus turns their honoring of the prophets against them. Their ancestors killed the prophets; they bury them. They treat the living prophets of their own day as their ancestors did (11:49).

decisions.choice: you build: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you build their tombs, as in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "their tombs" to complete the sentence. The shorter text is found in early manuscripts. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they did the killing, and you do the building
alternatives: they killed them, and you build
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sharp balance of the Greek.

decisions.choice: you show that you agree
decisions.reason: Readable says what being witnesses means here.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ εἶπεν· Ἀποστελῶ εἰς αὐτοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἀποστόλους, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ διώξουσιν, ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἅβελ ἕως αἵματος Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀπολομένου μεταξὺ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐκζητηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.
records.gloss: Because of this also the Wisdom of God said, I will send to them prophets and apostles, and of them they will kill and persecute, \v 50 so that may be required the blood of all the prophets having been poured out from foundation of world from the generation this, \v 51 from blood of Abel to blood of Zechariah the [one] having perished between the altar and the house; yes, I say to you, it will be required from the generation this.
pieces: That is why the Wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles. They will kill some of them and hunt down others.'
And so the blood of all the prophets shed since the world was founded will be charged to this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who died between the altar and the house of God. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be charged with it.

L.49: Because of this the Wisdom of God also said, 'I will send to them prophets and apostles, and [some] of them they will kill and persecute,'
L.50: so that the blood of all the prophets poured out since [the] foundation of [the] world may be required from this generation,
L.51: from [the] blood of Abel to [the] blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house. Yes, I tell you, it will be required from this generation.

R.49: That is why the Wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles. They will kill some of them and treat others cruelly.'
R.50: So the people of this generation will be held guilty for the blood of all the prophets killed since the world began,
R.51: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah. Zechariah was killed between the altar and the house of God. Yes, I tell you, the people of this generation will be held guilty for it all.

decisions.choice: the Wisdom of God: God's wisdom, speaking as a person
alternatives: the title of a lost book
decisions.reason: Scripture pictures God's wisdom as a woman who calls out to people and is refused (Proverbs 1:20-33; 8:1-36). The words that follow are not found in any book of the Old Testament. They may sum up God's purpose as Scripture shows it (2 Chronicles 36:15-16), or come from a writing now lost. In Matthew 23:34 Jesus speaks them as his own: "I send".

decisions.choice: the quotation ends after "persecute"
alternatives: the quotation runs on to the end of the list in 11:51
decisions.reason: The Greek has no quotation marks. The words of Wisdom may end at 11:49, with Jesus drawing the conclusion in 11:50-51, or include 11:50-51a. "Yes, I tell you" is clearly Jesus speaking.

decisions.choice: apostles: messengers sent out
decisions.reason: The word means people sent with a message. Here it stands beside the prophets as God's messengers (compare 6:13).

decisions.choice: the blood required: called to account for murder
decisions.reason: To require someone's blood is to hold the killer to account (Genesis 9:5; 2 Samuel 4:11). As Zechariah died he prayed that the LORD would see it and call it to account (2 Chronicles 24:22). This generation, which rejects God's messengers as their ancestors did, will answer for it all.

decisions.choice: Abel to Zechariah: the first and the last murders told in the Scriptures
alternatives: Zechariah the prophet of the book of Zechariah
decisions.reason: Abel's blood cried out to God from the ground (Genesis 4:8-10). Zechariah son of Jehoiada was stoned in the court of the LORD's house for speaking God's word (2 Chronicles 24:20-22). In the traditional order of the Hebrew Scriptures, Chronicles comes last, so the two murders span the whole of Scripture.

decisions.choice: the house: the house of God, the temple building
decisions.reason: Zechariah died in the court of the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 24:21), between the altar of burnt offering and the temple building itself.

decisions.choice: the world: the created world
decisions.reason: "Since the foundation of the world" means since the beginning of history.

decisions.choice: of God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose house it is.

decisions.choice: the words of Wisdom in single quotation marks inside Jesus' speech
decisions.reason: A quotation within speech takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: will be held guilty for
decisions.reason: Readable says what having blood required means.

records.source: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.
records.gloss: Woe to you the lawyers, for you took away the key of the knowledge; yourselves not did enter, and those entering you hindered.
pieces: How terrible for you experts in the law! You have carried off the key of knowledge. You have not gone in yourselves, and you have stood in the way of those who were going in."

L.52: Woe to you experts in the law, for you took away the key of knowledge; you yourselves did not enter, and you hindered those who were entering."

R.52: How terrible for you experts in God's law! You have taken away the key that opens the door to knowing God. You did not go in yourselves, and you stopped others who were trying to go in."

decisions.choice: the key of knowledge: the key that opens the way to knowing God
decisions.reason: The experts held the key to the Scriptures, which lead to the knowledge of God and of his salvation (1:77). By their teaching they kept it from the people. What the door opens on is not stated.

decisions.choice: those entering: those who were trying to go in
alternatives: those who had already gone in
decisions.reason: The present tense describes people on the way in, whom the experts stopped.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: the key that opens the door to knowing God
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture, following the first decision.

records.source: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι δεινῶς ἐνέχειν καὶ ἀποστοματίζειν αὐτὸν περὶ πλειόνων, ἐνεδρεύοντες αὐτὸν θηρεῦσαί τι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: From there having gone out him began the scribes and the Pharisees terribly to be hostile and to make him speak about many things, \v 54 lying in wait for him to catch something out of the mouth of him.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place, the scribes and the Pharisees turned bitterly against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kept pressing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with questions about many things,
watching for a chance to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own words.

L.53: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly hostile and to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} closely about many things,
L.54: lying in wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to catch something from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.

R.53: When Jesus left there, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees became very hostile toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They began to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} hard questions about many things.
R.54: They were trying to catch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying something wrong.

decisions.choice: scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: As in 5:21. The scribes studied, taught and applied the law; Luke also calls them experts in the law (11:45).

decisions.choice: be terribly hostile: hold a fierce grudge, press hard against him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Herodias's grudge against John (Mark 6:19).

decisions.choice: question closely: try to make him speak without thinking
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw someone out by questions, hoping for a careless answer.

decisions.choice: to catch something from his mouth: to trap him by something he says
decisions.reason: The words picture hunters lying in wait for prey.

decisions.choice: the shorter text, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: a longer text in some manuscripts, adding that they sought a charge to bring against him
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add that they were seeking to catch him so that they might accuse him, and one ancient manuscript tells the scene in different words. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today a scribe is someone who writes. Readable says what these men did.

decisions.choice: catch him saying something wrong
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.
